title: Video: Inter star Dimarco trains with knee bandage before Real Madrid clash
description: Inter star Federico Dimarco is training with the rest of the team this morning on the eve of a Champions League match against Real Madrid, but is wearing a knee bandage due to a mild strain sustained ...
fullText:
Inter star Federico Dimarco is training with the rest of the team this morning on the eve of a Champions League match against Real Madrid, but is wearing a knee bandage due to a mild strain sustained against Napoli over the weekend.

Italy international Dimarco began training with the rest of his Inter teammates today, but, as reported by FcInter1908, he has his right knee heavily bandaged.

PERTH, AUSTRALIA – AUGUST 08: Federico Dimarco of FC Internazionale celebrates his goal during the match between Juventus and FC Internazionale at Optus Stadium on August 08, 2026 in Perth, Australia. (Photo by James Worsfold/Getty Images)

Dimarco was forced to come off on Saturday during Inter's 3-2 win over Napoli due to a mild knee sprain.

Inter will visit Real Madrid in their 2026-27 Champions League opener tomorrow and will fly out to Spain in the afternoon.

MILAN, ITALY – MAY 03: FC Internazionale coach Cristian Chivu and Federico Dimarco celebrate after being confirmed as Serie A match between FC Internazionale and Parma Calcio 1913 at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on May 03, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

It remains to be seen whether Dimarco will be called up, and Cristian Chivu will provide the latest injury updates during a press conference in Madrid later today.

fullText:

title: Fulham 2-3 Crystal Palace - the fans' verdict
description: Tom: Who would have thought that replacing Premier League experience with novices on and off the pitch would backfire almost immediately?  If we don't win before the international break, then Alvaro Arbeloa will have to go.  Brian: We knew it would be a massive change from Marco Silva as the majority of players were/are his and that losing Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez would change the dynamics.
fullText:
We asked for your thoughts after Saturday's Premier League game between Fulham and Crystal Palace.

Here are some of your comments:

Tom: Who would have thought that replacing Premier League experience with novices on and off the pitch would backfire almost immediately? If we don't win before the international break, then Alvaro Arbeloa will have to go.

Brian: We knew it would be a massive change from Marco Silva as the majority of players were/are his and that losing Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez would change the dynamics. I can see what Alvaro is trying to achieve but it may take longer than some in the home crowd are prepared to accept. I'm not worried, there is too much quality in the squad, but we know football management is cursed, so let's see how it pans out.

Simon: Arbeloa's system can't defend but the board knew this when taking the gamble with him and the Real Madrid academy. This is a strategic error to chase player profits over Premier League stability. We've leaked seven goals in three league games. You can't stay in this division with that defence.

Russ: The managerial appointment was always going to be high risk but out of our supporters' hands. The manner in which we concede goals has to be a concern and with games against Liverpool and Manchester United coming up, this should have been at least our first point. Early days, but what I saw at Craven Cottage on Saturday is concerning.

Gary: It was great to get the win, but we are too open at the back and playing too high up the pitch. Offensively, we look good. The forward players need to be more clinical. We have Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta to come back, so I'm sure they will make the difference if they can get their heads right. I'm pleased for Tyrick Mitchell getting his first double. We have three home games now - games we should win. Hopefully, a good start in the cups and three points against Ipswich.

Steve: An entertaining game full of defensive frailties on both sides. One positive is that Palace scored three goals, but there is still cause for concern. Chris Richards was often caught out of position and Adam Wharton lacked control and dynamism. The team perhaps still needs time to gel, but a much-needed win is very welcome.

Derek: This win was huge, not only for the team and the new manager, but so important for the fans. Everyone's morale will be reinvigorated by this result. Must push on with ground improvements.

Andy: It was good to get the win in a competitive game. There are plenty of positives, one being the presence of Quinten Timber and the improved attacking intent of Tyrick Mitchell. Our defending appears chaotic, but this could be part of the new bonding process and could come good. We need to improve our distribution as we are giving the ball away too easily.

title: Pac-12 commissioner reveals why Colorado State fits the league's goals
description: Pac-12 commissioner Teresa Gould discusses the league's goals, power status and why Colorado State is a fit for the brand.
fullText:
Teresa Gould spent the weekend watching one of the Pac-12's newest members make its debut in the league.

Gould, the Pac-12 commissioner, was in Fort Collins for Border War weekend as the Colorado State football team beat Wyoming 35-13.

It was a notable result for the Pac-12, an on-field win in the lingering Pac-12 vs. Mountain West battle. Gould attended CSU's pep rally in Old Town the night before the game and saw a program record crowd at Canvas Stadium as the Rams won the Bronze Boot.

Ahead of the game, Gould spoke to a group of reporters on a variety of topics. Here's what she said about CSU and the Pac-12.

"You look around and when I think about the experience I've had here over the last 48 hours, the stadium is going to be packed today, there is fandom and passion in this community. I was at the pep rally last night and it was just incredible, the tradition.

"This is a college town and so CSU, it has an unbelievable elite institutional academic reputation, great leadership alignment with (president) Amy (Parsons) and (athletic director) John (Weber), great investment from the institution into athletics and a real desire to continue to build the tradition to be great and be competitive.

"This place is amazing and more people need to know about it. And that's where I think the Pac-12 and the association of Pac-12 hopefully can help elevate the brand because it's exactly what we are about in the new Pac-12."

"I personally was not surprised and part of that is a byproduct of I've been in the West for a really long time and so I was very, very familiar with CSU and the longstanding volleyball tradition and legacy and I have been around and followed CSU for a very long time.

"I also have the benefit of having a lot of family in the area. I have family members that are alums of CSU and have spent a lot of time in Northern Colorado and so I wasn't surprised. I will say, every time I come here, my kind of support and just admiration for what is here is, goes up. You know, I stood out on that plaza at the pep rally last night, and I'm like, this place is awesome. We need more people to know that. We need more people to see that and feel that and understand that outside of this region."

"Well, look, we've talked a lot about the North Star is having a team in the CFP (College Football Playoff), right? I mean, that is the pinnacle of college football. That is the investment that is being made across these eight programs, hiring these great legendary coaches like Coach (Jim) Mora and getting these talented athletes, everybody's trying to win a conference championship and get to the CFP, and so that is one of our metrics, and that is our North Star in Pac-12 football.

"I would also say it's critically important from a brand perspective that when folks either show up at one of our stadiums or turn on a television, that they see fandom, that they see communities who care about their programs, like what we're going to have today here in Fort Collins. We need to look like we matter in the college sports ecosystem, and we do.

"What you're going to see here today is very different than what we've seen on some of the TVs that we've turned on this morning and so the fandom and the crowd support and the attendance is really important, and then, of course, eyeballs always matter. We are fortunate that 50 out of 50 football games are on national television. All over the country, people can easily watch Pac-12 football and we are the only conference that has that.

"Part of that was an intentional and strategic decision to be able to demonstrate to the country that our product really matters and that it has significant economic value and so we need people to watch our games. So those are some of the measurements. We want butts in the seats. We want fandom in our stadiums. We want eyeballs on our games so that our viewership is representative of the strength of this league and team in the CFP, you know, five-plus teams in postseason bowls. Those are all the metrics that we're looking for."

"We are a top-five conference, right? I don't know what a power conference means. I don't know what autonomy conference means because nobody has defined that. Nobody has answered that question. What I know is the things that we control, which is butts in the seats, eyeballs on the TV, winning games, competing, that we are a top-five conference. The data shows that. The metrics show that, and that's what we're going to lean into.

"We don't control any of those other things. I don't control whether the NCAA decides to answer that question for me or not. I don't control what the folks on TV, how they refer to conferences. What we are leaning into is we're going to pave our own path and control what we can control, and this is a power league."

Sports reporter Kevin Lytle can be found on social media on X, Instagram and Threads @Kevin_Lytle and on Bluesky.

This article originally appeared on Fort Collins Coloradoan: Pac-12 commissioner reveals why Colorado State fits the league's goals

title: Phillies Former Outfielder Cut By New Team Shortly After PED Defense
description: The Philadelphia Phillies’ former outfield slugger has been cut from his new roster just a few days after offering an interesting defense.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Phillies' brief relationship with a long-time big league outfielder came to an end before he could establish himself as a long-term piece in the organization.

After spending the 2025 season in Philadelphia, Kepler entered free agency and then immediately faced an 80-game suspension that dramatically complicated his attempt to find a new opportunity.

Kepler eventually landed with the Arizona Diamondbacks at midseason, giving the former Minnesota Twins regular a chance to rebuild his value in the majors. Instead, his return to the field produced another difficult chapter shortly after he spoke out at length about his PED suspension for the first time.

Yankees, Red Sox Castoff Left 'Crying' After Sudden Move To Another AL East Rival

Kepler's brief comeback has now ended with another roster setback. The Arizona Diamondbacks designated him for assignment and recalled catcher Adrian Del Castillo from Triple-A Reno on Sunday, Connor Byrne reported for MLB Trade Rumors.

Even before the suspension, Kepler seemed unlikely to re-sign with the Phillies as he struggled to consistently produce during his lone season with the team. He hit .216/.300/.391 with 18 home runs in 474 plate appearances, numbers that translated to an 88 wRC+.

The 33-year-old remained unsigned until June while serving the suspension that stemmed from his positive PED test. Arizona ultimately gave him a major league opportunity on a prorated contract but his return did not produce the rebound the Diamondbacks hoped to see as they push toward a playoff spot.

After being activated on June 25, Kepler hit just .205/.262/.303 with two home runs over 145 plate appearances, resulting in a 53 wRC+ and a career-low .098 isolated power mark.

Kepler also struggled against right-handed pitching, an area where he had traditionally been more productive. During his brief Arizona stint, he hit only .192/.256/.283 against righties.

Former Dodgers All-Star Slugger Sets HR Record With Latest Team

Kepler's recent explanation for the suspension added another layer to an already unusual stretch of his career.

"Our theory, which we were trying to put together with my lawyers, was the fact that you can consume a steroid with contaminated red meat, which I was eating a lot of red meat at the time," Kepler explained to Phillies Nation's Destiny Lugardo last week. "Then again, even if you would have sourced the contaminated red meat, there's no chance that a company admits to contaminating their meat. So this theory was a theory, but it wouldn't really hold up. So a positive test is a positive test."

While Kepler defended his positive PED test as unintentional, observers could be taking note that his production picked up notably in the latter part of last season and then appeared to drop off when he returned this season.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Pro Football Focus details Texas A&M QB's successful 2026 debut
description: PFF provided Texas A&M QB Marcel Reed's day through the air on Saturday, detailing his deep throw grade and improved decision making when pressured.
fullText:
Texas A&M opened the 2026 regular season in dominant fashion, at least in the second half, blowing out Missouri State 50-0 on Saturday night thanks to an elite defensive effort combined with 236 rushing yards and six touchdowns, while redshirt junior quarterback Marcel Reed was highly impressive, completing 21/30 for 233 yards and 2 touchdowns, and a 75.9 QBR.

Per Pro Football Focus, Reed led all Texas A&M players with an 80.6 offensive grade and 78.6 passing grade, which, compared to last year's season opener, is a marginal improvement, especially based on PFF standards for quarterback grading. Looking poised in the pocket and delivering several NFL-level throws, Reed's offseason focus on fixing his mechanical issues resulted in his best preseason, confirmed by coach Mike Elko last week.

Some of Reed's best throws came behind the line of scrimmage and on 20-plus-yard deep throws, directing his receiver upfield on swing passes, while connecting with transfer wide receiver Isaiah Horton on multiple deep throws that showed off his improved accuracy and touch.

PFF released its Passing Pressure, Concept & Direction Report after Saturday's win, providing more context regarding Reed's success at every level of the field. According to the site, Reed was highly successful in play action, earning an elite 91.0 passing grade, while finishing 16/16 on behind-the-LOS and short throws and 4/7 on intermediate attempts.

When blitzed, Reed earned a solid 78.0 passing grade, making quick decisions to check down to the flat or use his legs to prevent a negative play. This version of Marcel Reed, combined with the offensive line continuing to improve, gives the Aggies a legitimate shot at returning to the CFP and competing in every SEC game at home or on the road.

title: What Oklahoma State football coach Eric Morris believes Cowboys must fix vs Oregon
description: Oklahoma State doesn't have time for avoiding the truth with No. 2-ranked Oregon coming to Stillwater on Saturday.
fullText:
TULSA — Eric Morris calls himself a truth-teller.

After Saturday's 24-10 loss at Tulsa, the Oklahoma State football coach sat in a sweltering interview room beneath H.A. Chapman Stadium and made a declaration.

"For a second year in a row, Tulsa, they reigned supreme on us right now on the football field," Morris said. "And that's a fact. I'm a fact guy, and I'm always going to tell you guys the way I feel."

After Tulsa beat OSU 19-12 a year ago in Stillwater, the Golden Hurricane backed up Tulsa football coach Tre Lamb's line about the rivalry from a February basketball game that Tulsa would, 'Beat their a-- again.'"

The Cowboys don't have time to dance around the truth. Problems exposed by a Tulsa team projected to finish middle of the American Conference must be corrected by 11 a.m. Saturday when No. 2 Oregon comes to town. Last year, Oregon beat OSU 69-3.

"And we got a lot of problems to fix, obviously," Morris said. "We got the No. — I don't know what they'll be — 1, 2 or 3 in the nation coming into town next week, and boy I tell you if they watch that film they'll be licking their chops."

More: Oklahoma State football best hope Drew Mestemaker is right after Tulsa debacle | Mussatto

Morris said the Tulsa out-coached, out-schemed, out-physicaled OSU. He added his play calls, specifically on the four fourth-and-1s OSU failed to convert were equally poor. Meetings to fix the problems started Saturday night.

Among the things Morris said he'll see on film: The offensive line didn't get enough push up front or protect off the edge without injured tackle Jacob Sexton, a still unresolved backup running back position behind Caleb Hawkins, an unnecessary roughness penalty after a third-down stop from Jaleel Johnson gave Tulsa a free second-chance touchdown and quarterback Drew Mestemaker "a little off" missing easy throws.

Morris was as blunt with his team in the locker room as he was with the media.

"He sat in there and said straight up that's the most embarrassing offensive performance he's ever been a part of, and I agree," Mestemaker said. "I mean, I'd say the same for me. That's just not how we play offense specifically. Defense, honestly, was the only reason we were in that game."

Along with the bluntness, Morris gave the players in his locker room another truth.

"That doesn't define our season at all, and that's exactly what Coach Morris said in the locker room," Mestemaker said.

OSU would know. Last season, The Cowboys won their season opener against UT-Martin and didn't win another game. In 2023, OSU lost at home 33-7 to South Alabama and rallied to win seven Big 12 games and reach the conference championship game.

"The last thing I'm going to do is lay down and forfeit the season," Mestemaker said. "That was one game and you know we have a great opportunity next week playing probably one of the best teams in the country. Obviously, it sucks and it's embarrassing, but you know by Monday and Tuesday it's got to be gone, and we got to be on to next week."

KICKOFF: 11 a.m. Saturday at Boone Pickens Stadium in Stillwater (ESPN)

Ben Hutchens covers OSU athletics for The Oklahoman. Have a story idea for Ben? He can be reached at bhutchens@oklahoman.com or on Twitter at @ben_hutchens_. Support Ben's work and that of other Oklahoman journalists by purchasing a digital subscription today at subscribe.oklahoman.com.

title: 'They're going to protect me': Texas A&M QB Marcel Reed praises O-line
description: Texas A&M QB Marcel Reed heaped praise on his O-line despite the unit's early struggles, sharing a close relationship with several starters.
fullText:
Texas A&M's offensive line struggled during the first half of Saturday's 50-0 shutout win over Missouri State, but improved in the second half, much to starting quarterback Marcel Reed's liking, as third-year coach Mike Elko and OL coach Adam Cushing made the necessary adjustments, leading to better communication at the LOS while paying close attention to their assignments.

At left tackle, LSU transfer Tyree Adams earned the third-highest Pro Football Focus grade (79.3) and was highly impressive in pass protection and run blocking, which is very important heading into Saturday's home matchup vs. Arizona State, while junior left guard Blake Ivy should retain his starting job, as his first-half struggles disappeared after halftime.

These blocking issues, after watching the tape a second time, stemmed from missed assignments, which was expected in the first game of the season after replacing four starters from the 2025 unit. Depth-wise, Elko could have certainly made drastic changes, but chose to stick with most of his original starting rotation, including South Carolina transfer right guard Trovon Baugh, who also struggled.

After the game, Marcel Reed discussed his close relationship with all his offensive linemen, including right tackle Wilkin Formby, Tyree Adams, and Blake Ivy, whose bond should help this revamped group protect their quarterback and play much better football for the rest of the season.

"I remember running out, and Wilkin Formby just said, 'I love you, brother.' I said, 'I love you, too.' Tyree Adams was checking in on me. I saw Blake Ivy maul somebody and get hype. They're going to protect me."

Mentality is everything as an offensive lineman, knowing that your central job is to keep the quarterback clean and open up holes in the running game. It's up to Adam Cushing to do his job and fix these remaining issues, which could lead to a change in the lineup, but right now, the second-half improvement shows this group is poised to improve.

"They said more to me. They tried to lift me up. Respect those guys a lot and the care they have for their quarterbacks. Those guys want to protect. I know they will get it done each Saturday."

Texas A&M will host Arizona State on Saturday, Sept. 6, which will air on ABC at 11 a.m.

title: Freiburg prodigy opts to switch allegiance from Tunisia to Germany
description: Louey Ben Farhat has decided to switch allegiance from Tunisia to Germany, according to Transfermarkt.The 20-year-old, who was born in the German city of Waiblingen, reportedly turned down a place in ...
fullText:
Louey Ben Farhat has decided to switch allegiance from Tunisia to Germany, according to Transfermarkt.

The 20-year-old, who was born in the German city of Waiblingen, reportedly turned down a place in Tunisia's World Cup squad, citing the heavy workload following a lengthy spell on the sidelines as one of the reasons.

The prospect of switching allegiance to Germany may also have played a role, with the attacker now expected to receive a call-up to the German U21 national team in September.

Ben Farhat joined Freiburg from Karlsruher SC for a reported €7.5 million fee this summer before being loaned back to the 2. Bundesliga side for the season.

title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan uses Australia time difference to dodge injury report
description: San Francisco is going to spend a week in Melbourne, Australia for the opener.
fullText:
Kyle Shanahan found a creative way to handle injury questions before the San Francisco 49ers' historic NFL season opener against the Los Angeles Rams. The game will start at 8:35 p.m. ET on Thursday in the USA.

Speaking from Melbourne, Shanahan joked that the massive time difference put San Francisco "in the future" compared with California. That allowed him to avoid giving an early injury update under the NFL's reporting schedule.

MORE: 49ers' Keion White opens up about 'trauma' of gunshot wound recovery

"Because we are technically in the future, and the Rams are in the present, I don't have to talk about injuries until tomorrow," Shanahan said.

The joke came while Shanahan discussed the difficulty of adjusting his internal clock. Australia sits 17 hours ahead of Eastern Time, creating unusual scheduling challenges for the 49ers.

"We're a little confused with when I look at my clock, and it says the time, and then I try to ​see my family's time, and it says the time, but it says yesterday," Shanahan said. "I don't get how that's possible. So I feel like I'm in the future."

San Francisco is going to spend a week in Australia preparing for Friday's local kickoff. The 49ers will face the Rams at 10:35 a.m. local time at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

That preparation matters because the Rams chose a different approach. Los Angeles plans to arrive shortly before the matchup, while San Francisco has focused on adjusting its sleep and training routines.

Inglewood, California, USA; San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle (85) talks with his teammate at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The injury situation makes Shanahan's timing joke more relevant. San Francisco lost defensive end Sam Okuayinonu to a fractured foot, while Nick Bosa and George Kittle have managed their respective recoveries.

The 49ers cannot afford major losses against a Rams team capable of stressing their defense and forcing long offensive possessions. Shanahan's approach also protects competitive information before the teams take the field.

Christian McCaffrey has praised San Francisco's detailed preparation for the unusual trip. Players received guidance covering sleep, nutrition, supplements and daily routines.

"There were big packets on the plane…," McCaffrey said. "So any questions ⁠you think you would have had, they answered it in these packets."

MORE: Daejon Love mug shot revealed after fraud arrest for impersonating 49ers player

Now, the bigger issue remains execution. The 49ers changed their routine to handle the international setting, but their roster still must perform under unfamiliar conditions.

Shanahan's comments added humor to an otherwise serious preparation week. Now, his players must turn that preparation into a strong opening performance against a familiar division rival.

title: Mourinho sees Real Madrid new signing as fully compatible with key defender
description: Jose Mourinho is considering a tactical solution that could finally give Real Madrid’s record signing Yan Diomande his first start while also allowing Trent Alexander-Arnold to move into a more cent...
fullText:
Jose Mourinho is considering a tactical solution that could finally give Real Madrid's record signing Yan Diomande his first start while also allowing Trent Alexander-Arnold to move into a more central role.

According to an update from AS (h/t Madrid Xtra), Mourinho believes Alexander-Arnold and Diomande can complement each other, with the teenager's presence on the right potentially allowing the England international to move inside and influence the game from midfield.

The idea could become particularly relevant when Real Madrid host Inter Milan in their Champions League opener, with Mourinho facing a depleted midfield and several difficult selection decisions.

Diomande has had a slow introduction to life at Real Madrid since arriving as the club's record signing.

The 19-year-old has made four league appearances but has accumulated only 83 minutes and has yet to start a match.

Diomande is yet to start for Real Madrid. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

Mourinho has been cautious with his integration, but the circumstances surrounding the Inter game could accelerate the process.

Arda Guler, Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga are all suspended, while Aurelien Tchouameni and Thiago Pitarch remain serious doubts.

The shortage of midfield options, thus, could force Mourinho to make changes elsewhere in the team.

That could open the door for Diomande to finally make his first Real Madrid start.

The winger's inclusion would also help facilitate Mourinho's plan for Alexander-Arnold.

Rather than remaining at right-back, the former Liverpool player could move into midfield and operate as part of a double pivot.

Alexander-Arnold could feature in the midfield. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

As reported before, the proposed midfield pairing would see Alexander-Arnold alongside Federico Valverde, with the Englishman taking responsibility for building attacks and Valverde providing the defensive protection and energy around him.

Alexander-Arnold's passing range makes the idea understandable.

From a deeper position, he would have more opportunities to dictate the tempo, switch play and exploit spaces with his long-range distribution.

His movement into midfield would also create room for Diomande to operate higher on the right.

At the same time, Denzel Dumfries could then occupy the right-back position, giving Mourinho a structure that accommodates all three players without forcing Alexander-Arnold to remain in his traditional role.

title: Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss passes for 336 yards, runs for 60 in 41-38 win in opener
description: Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who may prove to be among the most polarizing prospects in the 2027 NFL draft, is off to a good start to his final season of college football.
fullText:
Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who may prove to be among the most polarizing prospects in the 2027 NFL draft, is off to a good start to his final season of college football.

Chambliss completed 21 of 36 passes for 336 yards, with three touchdowns and one interception, and also added nine carries for 60 yards and a rushing touchdown, as No. 9 Ole Miss beat No. 24 Louisville 41-38.

A year ago, Chambliss was a little-known transfer from Division II Ferris State who wasn't even expected to start at Ole Miss, but he became more than just a starter. He became one of the best players in the country, leading Ole Miss to the College Football Playoff.

So why is Chambliss polarizing as a prospect? He's on the smaller side (listed at 6-foot-1, possibly shorter) and is already 24 years old and in his sixth year of college football, so he may have less less upside and room for growth than some of the younger, less experienced quarterback projects.

Will Chambliss be a first-round pick? A Day Three pick? There's a wide range of potential outcomes, but he can help his case by continuing to play like he did against Louisville.

title: Harvey Elliott might already be questioning what Giorgi Mamardashvili told him about Valencia
description: Harvey Elliott made his debut for Valencia on Sunday after joining the LaLiga side on loan from Liverpool for the season, but it wasn’t an occasion to remember for the 23-year-old.Having not even be...
fullText:
Harvey Elliott made his debut for Valencia on Sunday after joining the LaLiga side on loan from Liverpool for the season, but it wasn't an occasion to remember for the 23-year-old.

Having not even been in the matchday squad for Andoni Iraola's first two league games in charge of the Reds, the attacking midfielder needed a move elsewhere in order to boost his chances of regular game-time this term.

Upon arriving in Spain last week, he spoke of being 'grateful' for the opportunity to play with Los Ches, although his first appearance for Carlos Corberan's side ended in a 5-0 drubbing at home to Barcelona.

As per Liverpool Echo, there was audible booing from Valencia supporters towards the end of the game at the Mestalla, with club president Kiat Lim and owner Peter Lim being told to 'go home', and the players were called 'mercenaries' by a band of irate supporters outside the stadium.

Elliott said at his unveiling last week that Reds goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili had given him a taste of what to expect at the Georgian's former club, with the 23-year-old saying: "Giorgi told me the fans are incredible.

"When things aren't going well, they support you and are with you until the end; and when you win and play well, they're the best fans you could have."

(Photo by George Wood/Getty Images)

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The on-loan attacker might now be questioning that insight from Mamardashvili, based on the anger from the Valencia faithful during and after the thrashing by Barcelona, with many home fans having left well before the final whistle.

Elliott has come to a club who used to be regular Champions League participants but have become entrenched in mid-table in recent years, finishing between ninth and 14th in each of the last seven seasons and even flirting with relegation at some points.

The 23-year-old came off the bench in the 54th minute with his team trailing 3-0, and while he was unable to stave off a further Barcelona onslaught, he at least made an effort to contribute by winning both of his duels, making two tackles and completing 17 out of 22 passes attempted (Sofascore).

Valencia won't face teams at the same level as the LaLiga champions every week, although a wretched start to the season has left them bottom of the table with only one point from their opening four matches.

Elliott won the Premier League with Liverpool and is used to playing in the Champions League. He faces a rather different fight this time around, but if he can obtain regular game-time and help to instigate a turnaround in fortunes for his loan club, his 2026/27 campaign would be regarded as a success.

title: Police launch investigation after German judoka attacked by opponent
description: The police have launched an investigation as a complaint was filed for assault after German Olympic judoka Timo Cavelius was hospitalized after being attacked by JC Leipzig fighter Akaki Japaridze of Georgia. The incident happened following a Bundesliga fight.
fullText:
The police have launched an investigation as a complaint was filed for assault after German Olympic judoka Timo Cavelius was hospitalized after being attacked by JC Leipzig fighter Akaki Japaridze of Georgia.

The incident happened following a Bundesliga fight. Cavelius was hospitalized with a broken jaw and lost two teeth.

The German, who competes for serial champions Abensburg, was attacked by JC Leipzig fighter Japaridze after winning their second fight in a team event on Saturday.

Japaridze hit Cavelius three times with his fist, after Cavelius had made a celebratory gesture.

According to the police, Japaridze was no longer at the sports hall in Leipzig when authorities arrived and had already returned to the hotel. The Georgian fighter is reportedly back in his home country.

The Leipzig police confirmed to dpa on Monday that an investigation has been launched, stating that the individual is known to them and that there is no immediate danger.

At the same time, the sports' governing bodies are to take further steps. The International Judo Federation (IJF), the European Judo Union (EJU), and the Georgian Judo Federation have already been informed of the incident, according to the German Judo Federation (DJV).

Cavelius took part in the 2024 Olympics in Paris and is now preparing for the 2028 Games in Los Angeles. But he cannot garner important ranking points as long he is sidelined after the incident.

He underwent surgery and will miss the World Judo Championships next month.

title: Belgian FA still wants Balogun ban answers
description: Belgium's FA says it still wants answers about why Folarin Balogun was allowed to play against them at the World Cup.
fullText:
Belgium's Football Association says it still wants answers about why Folarin Balogun was allowed to play against their team at the World Cup - and have asked for the issue to be on the agenda at the next Fifa Council.

In one of the most controversial moments of the summer's World Cup, Balogun was cleared to play for co-hosts USA in the last-16 tie with Belgium after a one-game ban following a straight red card in his previous game was suspended for a year by Fifa.

That was a highly unorthodox decision and received widespread criticism, especially after it emerged US President Donald Trump and White House officials had lobbied Fifa.

European governing body Uefa and the Royal Belgian Football Association (RBFA) were among those to question the decision.

The RBFA said it had asked Fifa for "a clear justification of the decisions taken and details on how such situations will be handled in the future".

Balogun - who scored three goals up to that stage - started in the game, which Belgium won 4-1. The Red Devils lost to Spain in the quarter-finals.

In a statement on Monday, the RBFA said it now wants the issue discussed on the Fifa Council meeting on 15 October - and says it will not support Gianni Infantino's bid for a further term as Fifa president.

RBFA president Pascale van Damme said: "Two months after the events, our questions remain unanswered.

"Given the importance of transparency and clarity for all parties involved, we request the necessary explanations and, at the same time, wish to explore where improvements to the current processes are possible, so that similar cases can be handled in a clear, consistent and efficient manner in the future.

"Together with Uefa, the other confederations and the national associations, we remain committed to transparency in decision-making, strong governance and clear processes. We remain open to constructive cooperation, in the interest of the trust, integrity and future of football."

Balogun's red card was the 189th in World Cup history and only the second, after Brazil's Garrincha in 1962, to not serve a suspension.

Fifa never fully explained the decision, just citing "article 27 of the Fifa disciplinary code" which allows it "to fully or partially suspend the implementation of a disciplinary measure".

No other suspensions were lifted at the 2026 World Cup.

Infantino, who has been Fifa president since 2016, confirmed this week he will stand for re-election in March.

The Swiss has been under huge pressure after details of a now-abandoned plan emerged that sought to sell stakes in Fifa competitions, including the World Cup, to private investment firms.

Belgium's football governing body is the latest to join the growing list of those to say they do not want Infantino to remain in the role.

The RBFA added its two reasons for refusing to support Infantino were the Balogun case and the Fifa Forward Enterprise to sell those stakes.

title: Do Aberdeen's problems run deeper than the dugout?
description: Following an underwhelming start to the season that has yielded just one Scottish Premiership win and two goals from five league matches, head coach Stephen Robinson is feeling the heat from the Dons support.
fullText:
Do Aberdeen's problems run deeper than the dugout?

Following an underwhelming start to the season that has yielded just one Scottish Premiership win and two goals from five league matches, head coach Stephen Robinson is feeling the heat from the Dons support.

However, after a number of years of player and manager upheaval, Sportscene pundit Ryan McGowan suggests frustrations should be directed elsewhere.

Speaking on the BBC's Scottish Football Podcast, the Livingston defender said: "Aberdeen are a massive club. They're a club that should be in the top three or four in Scotland with the budget, size of club and fanbase.

"They should be right up there challenging. The fans have gone a lot of seasons now where they have probably not been looking forward to watching their team play.

"For the fans, that's all you just want: to be proud of your team. Of course, you want to see fast, attacking, attractive football, but you also want to just see a team that you identify with and have a real connection with.

"Over the past four, five, six seasons, they've really struggled with that."

On the decision-making at Pittodrie, former Hearts player McGowan added: "The turnover of players and turnover of managers - they just seem to be a club that's almost just making decisions on the spot.

"There's no real forward thinking. Even if you just look at the past three or four managers, they're all almost completely different styles, different nationalities, brought in with different experiences at different stages of their coaching careers.

"Albeit the pressure is on Robinson at the moment, I think a lot of their problems possibly run a bit deeper."

title: Bill Dundee Dead At 82, Memphis Wrestling Legend Passes Away (Wrestling News)
description: 'Superstar' Bill Dundee has passed away.
fullText:
In some sad news, the legendary 'Superstar' Bill Dundee has passed away at the age of 82.

Taking to Facebook, Bill's son Jamie - who wrestling fans may know as J.C. Ice of the PG-13 tag team - announced that Superstar passed away at 3:30 am Sunday. He had been battling dementia in recent years.

With a heavy heart ot hurts me to have to say this ...At 330 this morning the SUPERSTSR BILL DUNDEE has passed away ...I love you Dad illl catch you on the OTHERSIDE........

Born in Scotland and raised in Australia, Bill Dundee - real name William Cruickshanks - entered the professional wrestling business in the early 1960s and would arrive in the United States in the '70s, initially as a tag team with George Barnes, having success in Memphis and winning the NWA Mid-America Southern Tag Team Titles for the first time in 1975.

Dundee famously had a decades-long on-off rivalry with Jerry Lawler, with the pair spending years either teaming together or feuding against one another, often over the Southern Heavyweight Championship. Away from his time in Continental and the USWA, Superstar would compete for the likes of Championship Wrestling from Florida, Mid-Atlantic, Central States, the AWA, and World Class. He'd also turn up in WCW as Sir William in 1993, serving as the on-screen manager of Lord Steven Regal.

Bill Dundee would remarkably remain semi-active right the way through until 2019, and the final match of his career came in December of that year at the Bobby Eaton: A Night of Appreciation event, where he'd be on the losing side of an eight-man tag match.

Superstar continued to make sporadic appearances in recent years, even despite his ill health, including being honoured in person on the latest episode of Memphis Wrestling, which aired the day before his passing.

The thoughts of all of us at WhatCulture Wrestling go out to the family, friends, and fans of 'Superstar' Bill Dundee.

title: Chicago Bears legend Matt Suhey, best friend of late Walter Payton, dies at 68
description: Matt Suhey was a second-round pick who spent his entire 10-year NFL career in Chicago, mostly leading his Hall of Fame backfield mate to glory.
fullText:
Another member from the legendary 1985 Chicago Bears squad has passed.

Matt Suhey, the fullback and best friend of Hall of Famer Walter Payton, whom he so often led to daylight, died over Labor Day weekend. A person familiar with the situation confirmed Suhey's death to USA TODAY Sports. That person was granted anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter.

Suhey, who spent his entire 10-year NFL career in Chicago, was 68. The cause of his death, which has not been publicly disclosed, is currently unknown.

"I felt like my dad and (Suhey) really got close because they had to be on the same page," Jarrett Payton, Walter's son, said in "A Football Life," an NFL Network docuseries.

"Matt watched my dad's back, kinda like being a bodyguard or protector. He blocked for him, he took a lotta hits, making sure that my dad would get the glory. Matt kinda sat back in the background, very unselfish."

Payton, who died in 1999, 12 years after he retired as the NFL's all-time leading rusher, was the godfather of Suhey's son, Scott.

A beloved teammate generally, Suhey also presented former Bears offensive tackle Jimbo Covert during his induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2021.

Payton, Suhey, Hall of Famer Steve McMichael and former safety Dave Duerson are among members from the famed '85 Bears, arguably the greatest single-season team in NFL history and one that crossed over into popular culture, who have died in recent years. Chicago made the playoffs in five of Suhey's 10 seasons, a span that has clearly marked the franchise's most sustained stretch of success during the Super Bowl era, which began in 1966.

A second-round pick out of Penn State in 1980, Suhey played in 148 games for the Bears and started 100 prior to his retirement following the 1989 season. He rushed for 2,946 yards and 20 touchdowns during his career, roughly what Payton routinely produced in two years.

But Suhey was also a very effective receiver out of the backfield, catching 260 balls for 2,113 yards, including five touchdowns and 93 first downs over the course of his career.

Suhey rushed for 52 yards and the first touchdown in the '85 Bears' Super Bowl 20 rout of the New England Patriots, still the only time the century-plus-old organization has hoisted a Lombardi Trophy. Infamously, Payton did not score in that 46-10 runaway, an admitted oversight by head coach Mike Ditka.

title: Jersey Bulls Women knocked out of FA Cup
description: Jersey Bulls Women suffer the first defeat in their history as they lose 3-1 at Bognor Regis Town in the FA Cup first qualifying round.
fullText:
Jersey Bulls Women suffered the first defeat in their history as they lost 3-1 at Bognor Regis Town in the FA Cup first qualifying round.

The island side won every game they played on the way to claiming the league title in their inaugural English football campaign last season.

But the seventh-tier Bulls could not get past sixth-tier Bognor Regis on their FA Cup debut.

That was despite Sam Silva-Pinto giving them the best possible start as she fired in a superb strike from the edge of the box into the top corner after four minutes.

But the hosts drew level two minutes later thanks to Sophie Humphrey's close-range strike.

Ten minutes later Bognor were in front as Humphrey again pounced.

Bognor Regis continued to pressurise the islanders and were eventually rewarded when Lou Lou Robson made it 3-1 from a corner with 10 minutes to go.

Bulls will begin their league campaign next week when they travel to face Sutton United U23's in the South East Counties Women's Football League Surrey Premier Division.

On Friday, the Chiefs reached injury settlements with three players who were waived/injured during Sunday's final roster cuts. Quarterback Chris Oladokun, guard CJ Hanson and running back EJ Smith have all been waived from Kansas City's Reserve/Injured (IR) list.

Players with less than four accrued seasons who are cut while injured revert to a team's IR if unclaimed on waivers. An injury settlement has the player and team negotiate an estimated recovery timeframe and pay a prorated portion of base salary to cover the expected missed weeks.

The covered timeline rarely becomes public. After the settlement expires, Oladokun, Hanson and Smith will be free to join the active roster or practice squad of any of the NFL's other 31 teams. A return to Kansas City will not be possible for an additional three weeks after that.

title: 'We're not robots' - why US Open men's contenders have tumbled
description: The chaotic nature of the men's draw has been a sharp contrast to the relative calm of the women's - but anyone can still win the US Open titles.
fullText:
Talent, athleticism and commitment are not nearly enough to become a Grand Slam singles champion.

Possessing the confidence that you can beat anyone on the biggest stage - where the eyes of the world are fixed on you and there is no place to hide - is arguably the most important characteristic a player can have.

Unwavering belief. Or, as former US Open runner-up Taylor Fritz describes it, delusion.

Fritz is one of the current crop of leading men yet to get his hands on one of the sport's major prizes. The world number 10 is also one of the guys who has blown what looked like a golden opportunity to win this year's US Open.

With Jannik Sinner missing through injury, and Carlos Alcaraz making his comeback from his long lay-off, it felt like a tournament where the leading seeds could capitalise.

Instead, six of the top 10 perished by the fourth round at Flushing Meadows - including Fritz, who squandered a two-set lead against Argentina's Francisco Cerundolo in round three.

"It shows you how even the circuit is, how tight every match is, how difficult it is to win matches," said 24th seed Cerundolo.

"Anything can happen right now."

The dominance of Sinner and Alcaraz - who have won 10 of the past 11 Grand Slam men's singles titles between them - adds to the pressure.

Speaking to the Guardian earlier this year, 28-year-old Fritz said he believes he will feel an "emptiness" at the end of his career if he does not win a Grand Slam title.

World number two Alexander Zverev finally landed his first major at this year's French Open, but revealed afterwards he "could not sleep" and was "not eating" during previous Slam fortnights because of nerves.

Once he released the pressure valve, the 29-year-old German went on to reach the Wimbledon final - where he played freer but still lost to Sinner - and remains in the hunt at the US Open.

Zverev is scrambling through his half of the draw despite being far from his best, but the spectre of Alcaraz - who is getting better with every win - looms large.

"The two-horse race between Sinner and Alcaraz is not healthy for the tour," former Wimbledon champion Pat Cash told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"With every win, Alcaraz is becoming more of a favourite. Four months off, no matches and he could win the US Open."

Pressure is not the sole reason for the leading seeds tumbling in New York.

One argument is that the current top 10 - Sinner and Alcaraz aside - is weaker than it has been for a while.

Illness, injuries and fatigue also contributed at the final major of a demanding season.

Fourth seed Novak Djokovic's ageing body let him down in his shock first-round exit, while third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime put his second-round loss down to suffering dizziness.

Fifth seed Flavio Cobolli said he lacked energy in a third-round defeat, which he attributed to his volume of matches and New York's sapping heat.

Cincinnati champion Arthur Fils lost a tough opener against former world number three Stefanos Tsitsipas, while teenager Rafael Jodar - who has played more than 50 matches in his first full season on tour - looked drained during his first-round exit.

"The season is long. I think all the guys who performed well in the preparation tournaments have it more difficult here," said Belgium's Alexander Blockx, who knocked out French Open finalist Cobolli.

"We're all human. We're not robots. Every week is difficult. Especially at a Grand Slam where it gets even more physical.

"Mentally you have to really stay in it."

The chaotic nature of the men's draw has been a sharp contrast to the calm of the women's.

Eleven of the top 16 seeds reached the fourth round, led by two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka and Australian Open winner Elena Rybakina.

Neither dropped a set on their way to the last 16, while American pair Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff - seeded third and fourth - progressed without any serious scares.

French Open winner Mirra Andreeva and Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova ensured the top six seeds remained unscathed.

Two-time major finalist Karolina Muchova, Ukraine's Elina Svitolina and 2025 US Open runner-up Amanda Anisimova were the first top-10 seeds to be eliminated when they lost in the third round.

"It is great for the women's tour to have so many people who could possibly win," added Cash.

"Anyone can win at any time - doesn't that make it exciting?"

The past seven Grand Slams have produced seven different winners - a stark contrast to Sinner and Alcaraz's dominance - and leads to a school of thought that the current crop of top stars feel less burden than the men.

Everyone in the top 10 is a reigning Slam or WTA 1,000 champion, underlining their ability to triumph on the biggest stages.

The four leading players locked in a battle at Flushing Meadows for the top ranking adds another element to the dynamic.

Sabalenka has been the world number one for the past two years, but has recently suffered a dip of form which leaves her position under severe threat.

Rybakina is guaranteed to overtake Sabalenka if she reaches the semi-finals, while Pegula and Gauff could pounce if they win the title.

"Looking at the difference between the points in the top 10 compared to the men, you can see how the depth is pretty crazy," said Pegula.

"Everyone has been very consistent and makes it hard to a certain extent [to win a Slam].

"But then you know there's not one or two super dominant players where you feel like they have to lose in order for you to have a chance."

title: Barcelona youngsters to receive new Champions League Debut Patch against Feyenoord
description: Barcelona’s UEFA Champions League campaign will begin with a potentially memorable night for two of their younger players, as Hamza Abdelkarim and Brian Farinas could make their first appearances in...
fullText:
Barcelona's UEFA Champions League campaign will begin with a potentially memorable night for two of their younger players, as Hamza Abdelkarim and Brian Farinas could make their first appearances in the competition against Feyenoord on Wednesday.

For 18-year-old Abdelkarim and 20-year-old Farinas, it could be the start of a personal Champions League chapter, as they will have a new piece of UEFA memorabilia to mark the occasion.

As per Mundo Deportivo, both players are eligible for the Champions League Debut Patch, a new initiative introduced this season to recognise footballers making their first appearance in the competition.

Abdelkarim is registered on Barcelona's List A for the Champions League, while Farinas has been included on List B as an academy player.

If either player steps onto the pitch against Feyenoord, whether from the start or as a substitute, the blue Debut Patch will be attached to the Champions League Starball badge on their shirt sleeve.

The initiative has been launched by UEFA and UC3 in collaboration with Topps, giving first-time Champions League players a distinctive way to mark a milestone that can become particularly meaningful in a young footballer's career.

For Barcelona, Abdelkarim and Farinas are the two currently available squad members who could make their competition debuts on Wednesday.

The two players may not be the only Barcelona representatives to receive the special recognition this season.

As per the outlet, Jesse Bisiwu, who is registered on List A, and Ebrima Tunkara have already participated in the UEFA photoshoot and could potentially feature in European competition once available.

Several other academy players are also eligible for the initiative if they are called upon.

Brian Farinas and Hamza Abdelkarim could feature the Debut patch. (Photo by Timothy Rogers/Getty Images)

Jordi Pesquer and goalkeepers Eder Aller and Iker Rodriguez could all receive the patch should they make their Champions League debuts.

Notably, once a player makes his debut, the blue patch is removed from the match-worn shirt and certified. It is then securely packaged alongside a certificate of authenticity before being transferred to Topps.

The company will use the patch to create a unique collectable card, which will subsequently be signed by the player.

For Abdelkarim and Farinas, the first objective will be to get onto the pitch against Feyenoord.

But should either youngster achieve that milestone, their first Champions League appearance could eventually become a unique piece of football memorabilia.

title: Chelsea criticised for transfer decision that has helped rivals
description: Kai Havertz at Arsenal Raises Fresh Questions Over Chelsea Transfer StrategyKai Havertz came back to hurt Chelsea again, and that is the part that matters. Arsenal’s 2-1 win over their London rivals...
fullText:
Kai Havertz came back to hurt Chelsea again, and that is the part that matters. Arsenal's 2-1 win over their London rivals was shaped by a player Chelsea once had, then chose to move on. When that player delivers in a game of this size, the debate writes itself.

Joe Cole did not dress it up. He criticised Chelsea for letting a top-level talent leave and strengthen a direct rival. His description of Havertz as "world-class" cuts to the point. If that is the level of player you believe he is, selling him across the city looks careless. Selling him to a team chasing major honours looks worse.

Havertz was instrumental in Arsenal securing the 2-1 result, and that will sting at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea have spent heavily and churned through players, yet this is the sort of move that keeps coming back. Clubs can talk about squad balance, tactical fit and long-term planning, but football is ruthless. If the player thrives elsewhere, especially at a rival, the explanation sounds thin.

There is a broader issue here with Chelsea's transfer strategy. Talent has left, money has gone out, and clarity has often been missing. Havertz may not have been perfect at Chelsea, few were during a chaotic period, but quality was always obvious. Arsenal saw a player they could use. Chelsea saw one they could cash in on. Right now, Arsenal look smarter.

Mikel Arteta deserves credit for finding a role and structure that brings out Havertz's strengths. Arsenal have been more coherent, more settled and more demanding. That gives good players a platform. Chelsea, by contrast, are still wrestling with identity. Until that changes, stories like this will keep surfacing.

The uncomfortable truth is simple. Chelsea sold quality to a rival, and that rival has benefited. In elite football, those mistakes do not fade quietly.

title: How teenage keeper's van trip around Europe ended with new club
description: After setting out on a van journey to find a new club, goalkeeper Milo Beimers has signed for Viterbese in Italy in an unexpected turn.
fullText:
When Milo Beimers set off on a van journey around Europe to find a new club, the final destination was always unknown.

Along with his dad Kevin and their converted transit van, the plan was to travel about 2,000 miles from Belfast to Spain, and eventually into Portugal.

The 18-year-old former Glentoran goalkeeper had a number of trials lined up but no idea where the next step of his footballing career would be.

After 30 days on the road, Beimers has signed for Viterbese, who play in a medieval city an hour outside of Rome in Serie D - the fourth tier in Italy.

"There's been a lot of ups and a lot of downs, but in the end it's worked out and the risk has paid off," said Beimers.

"Living in a van is something new and I'll maybe never do it again, but we've learned a lot from it.

"I'm really proud to find a club and continue my journey in Europe."

Destination unknown - goalkeeper's 2,000-mile van trip to find new club

After he left Glentoran, where he had been from the age of 13, the initial plan for Beimers, his dad and their van was a 2,000-mile journey with a number of trials.

It was far from the traditional route to find a new club, and it is perhaps no surprise it took Beimers to an unexpected place.

He had a trial with Hercules in Spain, and then flew back to London for another opportunity but a call took him to Italy.

After one month on the road, the successful trial led to him signing with Viterbese to achieve his goal of finding a new club.

"When I came back from England, there was a week where nothing was happening and then suddenly I'm getting signed for a club," said Beimers, who is a Canada youth international.

"My mum always says life moves really slow and then it moves really quickly all of a sudden, and that's exactly what's happened.

"There was a moment of realisation whenever I signed that was just like 'I've done it'.

"You have all this stress built up. You have all these questions like 'why is this not working?' But then to suddenly sign is amazing."

Viterbese were relegated to Serie D last season and Beimers says part of the appeal is wanting to get them promoted back to the third tier.

For the new season they have merged with another club under the banner of Vigor Campagnano Gialloblu, but Viterbese is still their home and DNA.

But that was not the only thing that attracted him to the club, with the facilities, a 7,000-seater stadium and people behind the scenes also key.

"They've been through a lot in the history of the club, and the the people are a big thing for me. I care a lot about how it's like off the pitch.

"Sometimes you just have to go with it and go with your gut."

He wants to establish himself as first choice but his main goal is to help the team back to Serie C, which he says would be "amazing".

Beimers made his debut on Sunday and kept a clean sheet in a 4-0 win over Anagni.

Before he set off on his travels, Beimers had spoken of his dreams of facing Barcelona or Real Madrid.

Now, if the luck of the draw falls his way, he could face the likes of Napoli, Roma or either of the Milan giants in the Coppa Italia.

Eventually, he may even work his way through the divisions where big matches become a regular occurrence.

"That would be unbelievable. I don't think I've even processed that yet," he said.

"To draw against someone that big would be unbelievable. It would be one of the biggest matches in my career."

In the spirit of pushing himself out of his comfort zone, Beimers does not speak Italian while most of his team-mates do not speak much English.

He had initially intended to learn Spanish to help him integrate on his journey, but now Italian is at the top of his agenda with his new team-mates helping him out to help him settle in to his new home in Viterbo.

"The people are so welcoming and they are very open to teaching you stuff.

"I'm slowly getting to grips with it and every day I'm getting better."

On the pitch, he adds the coaching techniques are also something new to learn.

"The Italian style is so different, from the techniques, the way I dive or the way I catch corners.

"It's all new to me so it will take a bit of time to learn it, but I'm excited for it and I'm ready to learn.

"Football is its own language. It's not really the words you say, it's more how you say it. Everyone seems to understand it."

Beimers had hoped the adventure would bring him closer to his dad, who is a Canada-born video game designer, and he says he was "the perfect guy to do it with".

"It was a long trip with a lot of ups, downs and silly arguments over nothing.

"But it's been great and it definitely has brought us closer together. He's a huge part of my life and I've got to hang out with him, which has been great."

Beimers documented his journey on social media and as well as showing the ups and fun aspects of their trip, he was also open about the struggles that come from trying to forge a career away from home, such as home sickness and loneliness.

He says it was important for him to show that side of things, and he wanted to be honest about his experience and not just show off the ideal way of living.

"I missed my friends and family, it was difficult to be away from them.

"There was also the uncertainty of not knowing where you're going, not knowing if it's going to work.

"It's important to show that it can be hard, even when it looks great all the time."

And what about the van, the unsung hero of the journey that had become a travelling home on wheels for father and son?

Beimers and his family converted it after his sister, Charlie, purchased it when it was in "bad shape".

After three attempts to get it through its MOT, the van held up throughout the journey and it will remain in Europe for a new adventure - back with its original owner.

"Her original plan to was go all around Europe in it, and we were just borrowing it for the time being.

"My dad is flying back home and I'm staying here, but she deserves to have it back."

After successfully finding a new club through a unique method, Beimers hopes his journey will inspire other young players to try something similar.

"I've hopefully taught some people that if opportunities don't come to you, then you have to create them yourself.

"Hopefully when I talk about, 'oh, it's been lonely here', it tells people that it's not going to be easy.

"But anything you really want in life is not going to be easy, and hopefully it inspires others to do the same."

title: Allen's 'two illegal blows' sent Carty through 'loose ropes'
description: Thomas Carty's team claim "two illegal blows" and "loose ropes" caused the Irishman to topple out of the ring in a bizarre first-round no-contest against David Allen.
fullText:
Thomas Carty's team have claimed "two illegal blows" and "loose ropes" caused the Irishman to topple out of the ring in a bizarre first-round no-contest against David Allen at Croke Park on Saturday.

The co-main event before Katie Taylor's victory over Flora Pili lasted just one minute and 22 seconds as Carty, who was unable to continue because of a suspected concussion, took a blow to the back of the head.

A statement confirmed Carty, 30, is back home and healthy after spending time in hospital receiving a brain scan.

"After just one minute and 30 seconds of round one, Thomas Carty had received two illegal blows to the back of his head at Croke Park on the Katie Taylor undercard," the statement said.

"The second blow causing Thomas a momentarily lapse forcing Thomas to reach for the ropes to regain his balance and the loose ropes gave way, propelling Thomas head first out of the ring causing him to strike his head on a ringside table.

"In turn this caused Thomas a suspected concussion and unfortunately an end to this fight on instructions from the ringside doctor."

Doncaster's David Allen said on his Youtube channel that he will probably "speak to the boxing board and ask if it can be overturned to a win".

The 34-year-old claimed he was "a bit too strong and rough" for Carty and said he was likely to win, with the punch that ended the fight not intentional and was aimed to "clip him round the ear".

"When I'm heavy and fit, he weren't going to hurt me in a million years. So, I smiled at him and he didn't like that," Allen said.

"I'm not aiming for the back of anyone's head ever, but I am aiming about here [the ear]. It wasn't a big shot, I tried to clip him round the ear as I always do, and he's turned his head into it. It's gone round the back of the head.

"From there on, I don't know. It's not for me to say what's happened. He's a good guy, I do like him... I've caught him behind the head, not on purpose, he's turned into and he's gone through the ropes.

"At the time, I said to the referee, 'are you not going to count?' If that was in the middle of the ring I'd have won by stoppage. I lost my rag a little and said, 'look, he's jumped out the [expletive] ring.' I couldn't quite believe it, really, I was a bit shocked."

title: I can't relate to pressure Eala faces - Gauff
description: World number four Coco Gauff says she "can't really empathise" with rising Filipino star Alexandra Eala because "she has more pressure than I do".
fullText:
World number four Coco Gauff says she "can't really empathise" with rising Filipino star Alexandra Eala because "she has more pressure than I do".

Eala became the first Filipino to win a WTA singles title last month and has risen to 18th in the world rankings.

After losing to Iva Jovic in the third round of the US Open, the 21-year-old got emotional when talking about the huge support she gets from the Philippines.

Gauff will now meet Jovic in the fourth round and the 22-year-old American was asked if she can relate to what Eala, with whom she has played doubles, has to cope with.

"No, I can't at all, because she's the first Filipino player to break a lot of the barriers that she's done, especially on the female side," said Gauff, a two-time Grand Slam winner.

"When you speak of athletes from the Philippines, she's doing similar things to what Manny Pacquiao is doing for her country.

"I'm lucky to be from the US, where we had a lot of icons to look up to, people who have already broken down doors for me to be here where I am.

"I can't really empathise in that aspect. The only way I can is maybe just the hype of everyone expecting you to win every single match."

On her US Open debut last year, Eala became the first Filipino player to win a match during the Open era, and has this year reached the fourth round at Wimbledon as well as the third round at Flushing Meadows.

After Wimbledon, she returned home to a reception held by Filipino president Ferdinand Marcos in her honour at Malacanang Palace in Manila.

Eala won her second WTA 125 singles title at Birmingham in June before claiming her maiden WTA 500 title at the Washington Open, with Filipino fans and flags becoming more prominent at her matches.

"From the outside looking in, she has more pressure," Gauff added.

"I have a lot of respect for her and what she's doing, but I can't really empathise. I feel like she has more pressure than I do."
